Global SEMIS Daily - *Sunday* 

 

The Outlook For The Global A.I. Trade + Our Top Global SEMIS Picks Into Q4 + 2027

I think this is surely one of Most Important Calls that we’ve done so far this year.

- Not only did we have our 3 Global Sector Heads - BLAYNE CURTIS (US) + JANARDAN MENON (EUROPE) + EDISON LEE (ASIA) all together at the same time - but they did not hide their disagreements on the Outlook For The Global A.I. Trade ! 

- As I’ve said many times before - we certainly don’t hide it if there any disagreements between our Global Sector Heads across Global SEMIS - we celebrate these differences of opinion & we want to discuss them !

 

William.

 

If you’d like any of the new models that our analysts refer to in this call, please just let me know.

September 25, 2026

 

USA | Semiconductors

Blayne’s Bytes: Optical Model Update, Consumer Agents and CPUs, ON NDR Recap

We updated our Optical model as 1.6T ramps faster than expected, with AI transceiver demand approaching 180M units in C27 and 245M in C28. NPO design activity is accelerating, while meaningful scale-up CPO adoption looks further out. Elsewhere, Meta’s Muse and Anthropic’s Akamai agreement strengthen the CPU demand story. As always, reach out to TeamBlayne@jefferies.com.

 

Optical Industry Update – 1.6T Accelerating, NPO Projects Expand: Demand trends across the optical ecosystem remain highly positive, with our AI transceiver forecast now approaching 180M units in C27 and 245M in C28 as the 1.6T ramp progresses faster than previously expected. Investor focus has increasingly shifted toward NPO, with most hyperscalers and compute vendors exploring proprietary architectures as meaningful scale-up CPO adoption appears pushed into C29. While NPO design activity remains robust and should support continued growth across the ecosystem, roadmaps and eventual winners remain fluid. We also continue to see improving content opportunities for analog suppliers as the move to 1.6T drives higher TIA, driver, and photodiode content per transceiver - MTSI and SMTC benefit. Overall, 800G demand is holding up, 1.6T is accelerating, leaving optical capacity still struggling to keep pace with demand. Please see our full note HERE. If you would like a copy of our Optical Model, please reach out to TeamBlayne@jefferies.com.

Agentic AI Adds Fuel to CPU Demand: Over the weekend, INTC CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company can currently satisfy only ~50% of customer CPU demand, pointing to inference and the growing number of AI agents as drivers of general-purpose compute needs. Personal agents offer an example of how that demand could develop, with Meta’s Muse giving each agent a cloud-based environment in which to run tasks. Each Muse user is allocated 2 vCPUs powered by an 88-core AMD EPYC 9D64 (Genoa) processor or 126-core EPYC 9D25. The configuration is a positive readthrough for CPUs, the lack of visibility on concurrency makes it difficult to forecast the magnitude of incremental demand but our assumptions indicate 10s of thousands not 100s of incremental CPU demand. Consumer agents are still in their early stages, but Muse’s launch and Anthropic’s recent agreement with Akamai to support growing CPU workloads both strengthen the case for rising CPU demand. We continue to prefer AMD over INTC, particularly given AMD’s use of simultaneous multithreading ahead of its planned return in INTC’s Coral Rapids, but see agentic AI as a potential rising tide for both.

CXMT Reportedly Enters NAND Market (Trendforce), L/T Risk Emerging with N/T Supply Disciplined: Chinese DRAM supplier CXMT is reportedly planning to enter the NAND market, with a new NAND R&D production line under development in Beijing. The company has also begun discussing its NAND roadmap with potential customers, including a recently established startup focused on AI infrastructure and supercomputing storage applications. While CXMT's reported NAND entry could emerge as an incremental L/T supply risk, the project remains in the R&D phase, with commercialization and scale production still uncertain. We continue to see disciplined NAND supply-demand dynamics through C28, as most announced greenfield NAND capacity is not expected to come online until 2H28 or later, such as MU.
